messages:
linh: alerting — controller-manager leader-election flapping in us-central1. ~5 leader changes in last 7m, lots of GPU-provisioning jobs stuck Pending. Can someone grab apiserver/etcd logs? :eyes:

ash: seeing a spike in apiserver connection resets around the same time. etctd grpc write/response times jump to 2s+. might be network MTU-related (fragmentation) — tags show nodepool-gpu-us-central-1 has mtu=1500 but overlay expects 1440. :thinking_face:

mike: confirmed from node syslogs — a bunch of PMTU blackhole signs (ICMP unreachable filtered). kubelet->apiserver keepalives are reordering. past hour we've had autoscaler request loops: scaled up 6 GPUs, then many terminated as provisioning timed out. cost hit is visible on the billing dashboard. :money_with_wings:

linh: helpful log snippet from controller-manager: 
```
I0318 09:12:11.345678 1 leaderelection.go:242] failed to renew lease: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
I0318 09:12:13.678901 1 leaderelection.go:310] failed to tryAcquireOrRenew: failed to renew lease: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded
```

tess: nodes report frequent conn resets to etcd endpoints too. etctd metrics show leader election rate spike. suspect PMTU + overlay encapsulation (VXLAN) + intermittent egress firewall rules on a subset of hosts.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-3485 (severity: high) — tagging oncall.

ash: quick mitigation idea: 1) temporarily bump controller-manager --lease-duration to 30s and --renew-deadline to 20s to reduce flapping during noisy network, 2) set autoscaler cooldown to 15m for GPU pools, 3) cordon new nodes in affected nodepool so provisioning doesn't churn more GPUs. thoughts?

mike: +1 to cordon. we should be careful with lease-duration changes — longer lease delays failover if controller-manager actually dies. but for the current noisy network it's fine as a short term. runbook: patch kube-system deployment controller-manager with new args, monitor leader-election metric.

linh: applied cordon on nodepool-gpu-usc1-001..006, paused autoscaler via: 
```sh
kubectl scale deployment cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --replicas=0
```
will re-enable when we see stable leader history.

infra-bot: noticed a recent edge change — route-propagation rule updated in project/networking 09:05 UTC, affected subnets: subnet-gpu-usc1-a,b. rolling back rule for a/b might be the low-friction fix.

tess: can we confirm MTU mismatch? run: `ip link show` on a couple of nodes and check cni config (/etc/cni/net.d/*.conf).

ash: ran checks — host interfaces show 1500, cni config mtu is 1440 on healthy nodes but 1500 on the affected subset. so overlay encapsulation + host mtu=1500 causes some fragmentation that our packet path drops.

mike: plan: rollback route-propagation rule (infra) + set CNI mtu=1440 on affected nodes, restart kubelet/CNI agent. short-term: increase controller-manager lease-duration & pause autoscaler. mid-term: add MTU validation to node join checks and alert on CNI/host mismatches.

linh: agree. I'll coordinate rollback with infra and schedule a rolling CNI config update for the 6 affected hosts (in maintenance window).

tess: adding a postmortem checkbox: quantify cost delta from GPU churn (estimate spike ~8 GPUs x 1.5h = ~$150), timeline of route change -> symptoms -> mitigation, and create an alert for leader-election rate > 3/min.

ops-bot: change request filed: CR-2026-902 — rollback route-prop for subnet-gpu-usc1-a/b (owner: routing-team). ETA 15m.

mike: monitoring: keep an eye on metric `controller_manager_leader_election_renewal_failures_total` and apiserver grpc latencies. will post graphs in 10m. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

linh: thanks everyone — marking thread as the incident channel for now. ping here when rollback completes or if autoscaler should be re-enabled. :thumbsup:
